// data/civic.js
// The ONE module the app talks to for political and geographic data.
//
//   GEOGRAPHY (real, from the U.S. Census Bureau + city open-data portals)
//     fetchStack / resolveFromPoint  which layers of government cover a point
//     fetchBoundary                  the outline of one layer
//     loadChildren                   every county in a state / city in a county
//     fetchChildShapes               clickable state / county polygons
//
//   POLITICS
//     fetchRacesForPlace             what's on the ballot. REAL for the races in
//                                    data/candidates.js (Massachusetts 2026 so far);
//                                    SAMPLE placeholders for everything else.
//     fetchEventsForPlace            town halls, meetings, voting dates
//
// To plug in a real dataset (e.g. your Supabase tables), replace the bodies of
// fetchRacesForPlace / fetchEventsForPlace. Each race needs a `kind` (which
// layer of government decides it, see data/kinds.js) and the UI does the rest.
// Races for districts can be keyed on the jurisdiction ids in `stack`
// (e.g. "congress:4822", "school:4819650", "senate:48017").
//
// Every function is async so swapping in fetch() is a drop-in change.

import {
  racesForNode,
  eventsForNode,
  resolveByCoords,
  ensurePath,
  pathToNode,
  attachChildren,
  pathFromStack,
} from "./places.js";
import {
  identifyStack,
  fetchBoundary as censusBoundary,
  listCounties,
  listMunicipalities,
  childShapes,
} from "./census.js";
import { kindsForLevel } from "./kinds.js";
import { racesForState } from "./candidates.js";
import {
  makeHouseRace,
  makeStateLegislatorRace,
  makeSchoolBoardRace,
} from "./races.js";

// ===== Geography ============================================================

/**
 * The stack of government layers for a place. `level` decides how much to look
 * up (a state needs only country + state; a city needs everything).
 * @param {[number, number]} point  [lng, lat]
 * @param {"globe"|"country"|"state"|"county"|"city"|"district"} level
 */
export function fetchStack(point, level, signal) {
  const kinds = kindsForLevel(level);
  if (!kinds.length) return Promise.resolve({ stack: [], inUS: true, point });
  return identifyStack(point[0], point[1], { kinds, signal });
}

/**
 * Resolve a coordinate (search result or GPS) to a path in the place tree.
 * @param {number} downTo  deepest level wanted: "state" | "county" | "city"
 * @returns {Promise<{path: object[], stack: object[], unincorporated: boolean,
 *                    unincorporatedName: string|null}>}
 *   path is just [Earth] when the point is not in the U.S.
 */
export async function resolveFromPoint(lng, lat, downTo = "city") {
  const res = await identifyStack(lng, lat, { kinds: kindsForLevel(downTo) });
  if (!res.inUS) return { path: pathToNode("globe"), stack: [], unincorporated: false };
  return {
    path: pathFromStack(res.stack, downTo),
    stack: res.stack,
    unincorporated: res.unincorporated,
    unincorporatedName: res.unincorporatedName,
  };
}

export function fetchBoundary(jurisdiction) {
  return censusBoundary(jurisdiction);
}

// Fill in a node's children from the Census: a state's counties, a county's
// cities and towns. Safe to call repeatedly.
const loading = new Map();
export function loadChildren(node) {
  if (node.childrenState === "loaded") return Promise.resolve();
  if (loading.has(node.id)) return loading.get(node.id);

  let job = null;
  if (node.level === "state" && node.geoid) {
    job = listCounties(node.geoid).then((items) => attachChildren(node, items, "county"));
  } else if (node.level === "county" && node.geoid) {
    job = listMunicipalities({ geoid: node.geoid }).then((items) =>
      attachChildren(node, items, "city")
    );
  }
  if (!job) return Promise.resolve();

  node.childrenState = "loading";
  const wrapped = job
    .catch((err) => {
      console.warn(`Could not load places inside ${node.name}:`, err);
      node.childrenState = "error";
    })
    .finally(() => loading.delete(node.id));
  loading.set(node.id, wrapped);
  return wrapped;
}

/**
 * Clickable outlines for the places directly below a node: every state (from
 * the U.S. view) or every county (from a state). Null for other levels.
 */
export async function fetchChildShapes(node) {
  try {
    if (node.level === "country") return await childShapes("states");
    if (node.level === "state" && node.geoid) return await childShapes("counties", node.geoid);
  } catch (err) {
    console.warn("Could not load outlines:", err);
  }
  return null;
}

// Fallbacks used only when the Census service can't be reached.
export async function resolvePlaceFromGeocode(desc) {
  return ensurePath(desc);
}
export async function resolvePlaceByCoords(lng, lat) {
  return resolveByCoords(lng, lat);
}
export async function fetchPathForPlace(placeId) {
  return pathToNode(placeId);
}

// ===== Politics (sample data today) ========================================

/**
 * Everything on the ballot for a place: races attached to the place (and its
 * ancestors) plus, for every district in `stack`, the office that district
 * elects. Each race has a `kind` (layer of government) and a `source`.
 *
 * @param {string} placeId
 * @param {object[]} [stack]  from fetchStack (empty is fine)
 */
export async function fetchRacesForPlace(placeId, stack = []) {
  const curated = racesForNode(placeId);

  // Real candidates (data/candidates.js) for the place's state, when we have them.
  const stateNode = pathToNode(placeId).find((n) => n.level === "state");
  const real = stateNode
    ? racesForState(stateNode.code).map((r) => ({
        ...r,
        scopeName: stateNode.name,
        scopeLevel: "state",
      }))
    : [];
  const state = stack.find((j) => j.kind === "state");
  const generated = [];
  for (const j of stack) {
    let race = null;
    if (j.kind === "congress") race = makeHouseRace(j.short);
    else if (j.kind === "senate") race = makeStateLegislatorRace("senate", j.name, state?.name || "the state");
    else if (j.kind === "house") race = makeStateLegislatorRace("house", j.name, state?.name || "the state");
    else if (j.kind === "school") {
      race = makeSchoolBoardRace(`${j.name} board`, `the public schools in ${j.name}`);
    }
    if (race) {
      generated.push({
        ...race,
        id: `gen-${j.id}`,
        jurisdictionId: j.id,
        scopeName: j.name,
        scopeLevel: j.kind,
      });
    }
  }
  return [...real, ...curated, ...generated].map((r) => ({ source: "sample", ...r }));
}

/**
 * Upcoming civic events for a place (own + inherited), soonest first.
 * Each: { id, title, kind?, type, start, end?, venue, virtual, description,
 * url?, source, scopeName }.
 */
export async function fetchEventsForPlace(placeId) {
  return eventsForNode(placeId);
}

// data/census.js
// U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb client: the source of real boundaries for every
// state, county, city/town, congressional district, state legislative district
// and school district in the country.
//
//   https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/
//
// Free, no API key, and allows browser requests (CORS). Layer IDs change as
// the Census adds new vintages (e.g. "120th Congressional Districts"), so they
// are looked up by NAME at runtime, with known IDs as a fallback.
//
// WHAT THIS GIVES THE APP
//   identifyStack(lng, lat)   -> every government layer covering a point
//   fetchBoundary(j)          -> the outline of one of those layers (GeoJSON)
//   listCounties(stateFips)   -> all counties in a state
//   listMunicipalities(county)-> all cities / towns in a county
//   childShapes(...)          -> clickable polygons for all states / a state's counties
//
// BOUNDARY CAVEAT: congressional and legislative maps are whatever the Census
// has published. States that redrew maps for 2026 may be ahead of (or behind)
// the Census data, so the UI tells people to confirm with their election office.

import { KIND_ORDER } from "./kinds.js";
import { findLocalLayers } from "./local-sources.js";

// TIGERweb has one MapServer per vintage. Most layers come from "Current"
// (120th Congress, 2026 legislative districts); voting districts (precincts and
// wards) are only published with the 2020 Census.
const SERVICES = {
  current:
    "https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/tigerWMS_Current/MapServer",
  census2020:
    "https://tigerweb.geo.census.gov/arcgis/rest/services/TIGERweb/tigerWMS_Census2020/MapServer",
};

// Layer IDs change as the Census adds vintages, so they are looked up by NAME at
// runtime; `id` is the fallback if that lookup fails.
const LAYERS = {
  states: { service: "current", id: 80, pattern: /^States$/ },
  counties: { service: "current", id: 82, pattern: /^Counties$/ },
  congress: { service: "current", id: 54, pattern: /^\d+(st|nd|rd|th) Congressional Districts$/ },
  senate: { service: "current", id: 56, pattern: /State Legislative Districts - Upper$/ },
  house: { service: "current", id: 58, pattern: /State Legislative Districts - Lower$/ },
  unified: { service: "current", id: 14, pattern: /^Unified School Districts$/ },
  secondary: { service: "current", id: 16, pattern: /^Secondary School Districts$/ },
  elementary: { service: "current", id: 18, pattern: /^Elementary School Districts$/ },
  places: { service: "current", id: 28, pattern: /^Incorporated Places$/ },
  cdp: { service: "current", id: 30, pattern: /^Census Designated Places$/ },
  subdivisions: { service: "current", id: 22, pattern: /^County Subdivisions$/ },
  vtd: { service: "census2020", id: 58, pattern: /^Voting Districts$/ },
};

// States where towns/townships (county subdivisions) are the real local
// governments. Everywhere else, incorporated places are.
const STRONG_MCD_STATES = new Set([
  "09", "23", "25", "26", "27", "33", "34", "36", "42", "44", "50", "55",
]);

// How much to simplify each outline (degrees). Bigger = smaller download.
const SIMPLIFY = {
  state: 0.02,
  county: 0.004,
  congress: 0.004,
  senate: 0.003,
  house: 0.002,
  city: 0.0008,
  school: 0.0015,
  ward: 0.0005,
  precinct: 0.0003,
};

// ----- Plumbing --------------------------------------------------------------

const memo = new Map();
function remember(key, make) {
  if (!memo.has(key)) {
    const p = make().catch((err) => {
      memo.delete(key); // never cache failures
      throw err;
    });
    memo.set(key, p);
  }
  return memo.get(key);
}

// One request, with a timeout. Census services are public and occasionally slow,
// so a failed attempt is retried once before giving up (the UI then falls back
// gracefully; see the "error" state of the layer dock).
const TIMEOUT_MS = 12000;

async function getJsonOnce(url, signal) {
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), TIMEOUT_MS);
  const onAbort = () => ctrl.abort();
  signal?.addEventListener("abort", onAbort);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ctrl.signal });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Census service error (${res.status})`);
    const data = await res.json();
    if (data.error) throw new Error(data.error.message || "Census query failed");
    return data;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
    signal?.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort);
  }
}

async function getJson(url, signal) {
  try {
    return await getJsonOnce(url, signal);
  } catch (err) {
    if (signal?.aborted) throw err; // the caller cancelled: don't retry
    return getJsonOnce(url, signal); // one retry
  }
}

function resolveLayers() {
  return remember("layers", async () => {
    const found = {};
    await Promise.all(
      Object.keys(SERVICES).map(async (svcKey) => {
        try {
          const svc = await getJson(`${SERVICES[svcKey]}?f=json`);
          found[svcKey] = svc.layers || [];
        } catch {
          found[svcKey] = [];
        }
      })
    );
    const out = {};
    for (const [key, def] of Object.entries(LAYERS)) {
      const hit = (found[def.service] || []).find(
        (l) => def.pattern.test(l.name) && !/Labels$/.test(l.name)
      );
      out[key] = { url: SERVICES[def.service], id: hit ? hit.id : def.id };
    }
    return out;
  });
}

async function query(layerKey, params, signal) {
  const layers = await resolveLayers();
  const { url: base, id } = layers[layerKey];
  const url = new URL(`${base}/${id}/query`);
  const all = { f: "json", outSR: "4326", ...params };
  for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(all)) url.searchParams.set(k, v);
  return getJson(url.toString(), signal);
}

const pointParams = (lng, lat) => ({
  geometry: `${lng},${lat}`,
  geometryType: "esriGeometryPoint",
  inSR: "4326",
  spatialRel: "esriSpatialRelIntersects",
  outFields: "*",
  returnGeometry: "false",
});

const num = (v) => {
  const n = parseFloat(v);
  return Number.isFinite(n) ? n : null;
};

const titleCase = (s) => s.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + s.slice(1);

// "Medford city" -> { name: "Medford", type: "City" }
function splitMunicipalName(attrs) {
  const full = String(attrs.NAME || "");
  const base = String(attrs.BASENAME || full);
  const rest = full.startsWith(base) ? full.slice(base.length).trim() : "";
  return { name: base, type: rest ? titleCase(rest) : "" };
}

function ordinal(n) {
  const s = ["th", "st", "nd", "rd"];
  const v = n % 100;
  return n + (s[(v - 20) % 10] || s[v] || s[0]);
}

function districtLabel(stusab, base) {
  const clean = String(base || "").trim();
  if (!clean || /^0+$/.test(clean) || /at.?large/i.test(clean)) {
    return { short: `${stusab}-AL`, name: `U.S. House: ${stusab} At-Large` };
  }
  if (/^98$/.test(clean)) {
    return { short: `${stusab}-DEL`, name: "U.S. House: Delegate seat" };
  }
  const n = String(parseInt(clean, 10));
  return {
    short: `${stusab}-${n}`,
    name: `U.S. House: ${stusab}-${n} (${ordinal(parseInt(clean, 10))} District)`,
  };
}

// ----- The stack: every layer of government at a point ---------------------

/**
 * @typedef {Object} Jurisdiction
 * @property {string} id         e.g. "county:48157"
 * @property {string} kind       key of KINDS (data/kinds.js)
 * @property {string} name       "Fort Bend County"
 * @property {string} [short]    compact label for chips: "TX-22"
 * @property {string} [type]     "City", "Town", "Unified school district"...
 * @property {string} geoid      Census id (or the local source's id)
 * @property {string} [state]    2-digit state FIPS
 * @property {[number, number]} [center] [lng, lat] inside the area
 * @property {string} [layer]    internal: Census layer key for boundaries
 * @property {object} [geometry] GeoJSON geometry when already loaded
 * @property {string} [source]   where the data came from
 */

/**
 * Every layer of government covering a point.
 *
 * @param {number} lng
 * @param {number} lat
 * @param {{kinds?: string[], signal?: AbortSignal}} [opts]
 * @returns {Promise<{stack: Jurisdiction[], unincorporated: boolean,
 *                    unincorporatedName: string|null, inUS: boolean,
 *                    point: [number, number]}>}
 */
export function identifyStack(lng, lat, opts = {}) {
  const kinds = opts.kinds || KIND_ORDER;
  const key = `stack:${lng.toFixed(4)},${lat.toFixed(4)}:${kinds.join("+")}`;
  return remember(key, () => doIdentify(lng, lat, kinds, opts.signal));
}

async function doIdentify(lng, lat, kinds, signal) {
  const wants = (k) => kinds.includes(k);
  const q = (layer, extra = {}) =>
    query(layer, { ...pointParams(lng, lat), ...extra }, signal).then(
      (d) => d.features || []
    );

  const [state, county, congress, senate, house, unified, secondary, elementary, places, subs, cdp, vtd] =
    await Promise.all([
      q("states"),
      wants("county") ? q("counties") : [],
      wants("congress") ? q("congress") : [],
      wants("senate") ? q("senate") : [],
      wants("house") ? q("house") : [],
      wants("school") ? q("unified") : [],
      wants("school") ? q("secondary") : [],
      wants("school") ? q("elementary") : [],
      wants("city") ? q("places") : [],
      wants("city") ? q("subdivisions") : [],
      wants("city") ? q("cdp") : [],
      // Voting districts are a separate (2020) service; a failure must not
      // break the rest of the stack.
      wants("precinct") ? q("vtd").catch(() => []) : [],
    ]);

  const point = [lng, lat];
  if (!state.length) return { stack: [], unincorporated: false, inUS: false, point };

  const sa = state[0].attributes;
  const stusab = sa.STUSAB;
  const fips = sa.STATE;
  const stack = [];
  const push = (kind, a, fields) =>
    stack.push({
      id: `${kind}:${a.GEOID}`,
      kind,
      geoid: a.GEOID,
      state: fips,
      center: [num(a.INTPTLON) ?? num(a.CENTLON), num(a.INTPTLAT) ?? num(a.CENTLAT)],
      source: "U.S. Census Bureau (TIGERweb)",
      ...fields,
    });

  if (wants("country")) {
    stack.push({
      id: "country:US",
      kind: "country",
      geoid: "US",
      name: "United States",
      short: "USA",
      center: [-98.5, 39.8],
      source: "built in",
    });
  }
  if (wants("state")) push("state", sa, { name: sa.NAME, short: stusab, layer: "states" });
  if (county[0]) push("county", county[0].attributes, { name: county[0].attributes.NAME, layer: "counties" });
  if (congress[0]) {
    const a = congress[0].attributes;
    push("congress", a, { ...districtLabel(stusab, a.BASENAME), layer: "congress" });
  }
  if (senate[0]) {
    const a = senate[0].attributes;
    push("senate", a, { name: a.NAME, short: shortDistrict(a.BASENAME), layer: "senate" });
  }
  if (house[0]) {
    const a = house[0].attributes;
    push("house", a, { name: a.NAME, short: shortDistrict(a.BASENAME), layer: "house" });
  }
  for (const [list, layer, type] of [
    [unified, "unified", "Unified"],
    [elementary, "elementary", "Elementary"],
    [secondary, "secondary", "Secondary"],
  ]) {
    for (const f of list) {
      push("school", f.attributes, {
        name: f.attributes.NAME,
        type: `${type} school district`,
        layer,
      });
    }
  }

  // City / town: incorporated place and/or county subdivision (see top note).
  let unincorporated = false;
  let unincorporatedName = null;
  if (wants("city")) {
    const strong = STRONG_MCD_STATES.has(fips);
    const mcd = subs.find((f) => f.attributes.FUNCSTAT !== "S");
    const place = places[0];
    const found = [];
    if (place) {
      const { name, type } = splitMunicipalName(place.attributes);
      found.push({ a: place.attributes, name, type, layer: "places" });
    }
    if (strong && mcd) {
      const { name, type } = splitMunicipalName(mcd.attributes);
      const same = found.find((c) => c.name.toLowerCase() === name.toLowerCase());
      if (same) {
        // Same government listed twice (e.g. "Medford city"): keep the
        // county-subdivision record in New England-style states.
        same.a = mcd.attributes;
        same.layer = "subdivisions";
      } else {
        found.push({ a: mcd.attributes, name, type, layer: "subdivisions" });
      }
    }
    for (const c of found) push("city", c.a, { name: c.name, type: c.type, layer: c.layer });
    unincorporated = found.length === 0;
    if (unincorporated && cdp[0]) {
      unincorporatedName = splitMunicipalName(cdp[0].attributes).name;
    }
  }

  // Voting precinct / ward (Census 2020 voting districts)
  if (vtd[0]) {
    const a = vtd[0].attributes;
    const { name, short } = formatPrecinct(a, fips);
    push("precinct", a, { name, short, layer: "vtd" });
  }

  // Wards / council districts from city open-data portals (see local-sources.js)
  if (wants("ward")) {
    const city = stack.find((j) => j.kind === "city");
    if (city) {
      try {
        stack.push(...(await findLocalLayers(city, fips, lng, lat)));
      } catch (err) {
        console.warn("Local ward lookup failed:", err);
      }
    }
  }

  const order = (j) => KIND_ORDER.indexOf(j.kind);
  stack.sort((a, b) => order(a) - order(b));
  return { stack, unincorporated, unincorporatedName, inUS: true, point };
}

// Turn a raw Census voting-district name into something readable. Ported from
// the Ward-Layer prototype (prototypes/ward-layer/script.js) and extended.
//   Massachusetts encodes ward + precinct as "WWPP": "0306" -> Ward 3, Precinct 6
//   Other states use a precinct number ("004042") or free text ("Wd 42 Pct 10").
function formatPrecinct(attrs, stateFips) {
  const raw = String(attrs.BASENAME || attrs.NAME || "").trim();
  if (!raw) return { name: "Voting precinct", short: "Precinct" };
  if (stateFips === "25" && /^\d{4}$/.test(raw)) {
    const ward = parseInt(raw.slice(0, 2), 10);
    const pct = parseInt(raw.slice(2), 10);
    return ward > 0
      ? { name: `Ward ${ward}, Precinct ${pct}`, short: `W${ward} · P${pct}` }
      : { name: `Precinct ${pct}`, short: `Precinct ${pct}` };
  }
  if (/^\d+$/.test(raw)) {
    const n = String(parseInt(raw, 10));
    return { name: `Precinct ${n}`, short: `Precinct ${n}` };
  }
  const name = raw
    .replace(/\bWd\.?\b/gi, "Ward")
    .replace(/\bPct\.?\b/gi, "Precinct")
    .replace(/\s+/g, " ");
  // "Medford City Ward 8 Precinct 1" -> chip label "W8 · P1"
  const ward = /\bward\s+(\w+)/i.exec(name);
  const pct = /\bprecinct\s+(\w+)/i.exec(name);
  if (ward && pct) return { name, short: `W${ward[1]} · P${pct[1]}` };
  if (pct) return { name, short: `Precinct ${pct[1]}` };
  return { name, short: shortDistrict(name) };
}

function shortDistrict(base) {
  const b = String(base || "");
  return b.length > 14 ? b.slice(0, 13) + "…" : b;
}

// ----- Boundaries -------------------------------------------------------------

/**
 * GeoJSON geometry for one jurisdiction (cached). Returns null for the country
 * (too large to draw usefully) or if the lookup fails.
 * @param {Jurisdiction} j
 */
export function fetchBoundary(j) {
  if (j.geometry) return Promise.resolve(j.geometry);
  if (j.kind === "country" || !j.layer) return Promise.resolve(null);
  return remember(`boundary:${j.id}`, async () => {
    const data = await query(j.layer, {
      where: `GEOID='${j.geoid}'`,
      outFields: "GEOID",
      returnGeometry: "true",
      maxAllowableOffset: String(SIMPLIFY[j.kind] ?? 0.002),
      f: "geojson",
    });
    return data.features?.[0]?.geometry || null;
  }).catch(() => null);
}

// ----- Lists for menus and clickable shapes ----------------------------------

/** All counties (or county equivalents) in a state, A to Z. */
export function listCounties(stateFips) {
  return remember(`counties:${stateFips}`, async () => {
    const d = await query("counties", {
      where: `STATE='${stateFips}'`,
      outFields: "GEOID,NAME,BASENAME,INTPTLAT,INTPTLON,CENTLAT,CENTLON",
      returnGeometry: "false",
      orderByFields: "NAME",
      resultRecordCount: "500",
    });
    return (d.features || []).map((f) => ({
      geoid: f.attributes.GEOID,
      name: f.attributes.NAME,
      center: [
        num(f.attributes.INTPTLON) ?? num(f.attributes.CENTLON),
        num(f.attributes.INTPTLAT) ?? num(f.attributes.CENTLAT),
      ],
    }));
  });
}

/**
 * Cities and towns in a county.
 * - New England-style states: the county's towns (county subdivisions).
 * - Elsewhere: incorporated places whose internal point lies in the county.
 * @param {{geoid: string, state?: string}} county
 */
export function listMunicipalities(county) {
  return remember(`munis:${county.geoid}`, async () => {
    const stateFips = county.geoid.slice(0, 2);
    const countyFips = county.geoid.slice(2);
    const fields = "GEOID,NAME,BASENAME,FUNCSTAT,INTPTLAT,INTPTLON,CENTLAT,CENTLON";
    const toItem = (a) => {
      const { name, type } = splitMunicipalName(a);
      return {
        geoid: a.GEOID,
        name,
        type,
        layer: "places",
        center: [num(a.INTPTLON) ?? num(a.CENTLON), num(a.INTPTLAT) ?? num(a.CENTLAT)],
      };
    };

    if (STRONG_MCD_STATES.has(stateFips)) {
      const d = await query("subdivisions", {
        where: `STATE='${stateFips}' AND COUNTY='${countyFips}'`,
        outFields: fields,
        returnGeometry: "false",
        orderByFields: "NAME",
        resultRecordCount: "500",
      });
      return (d.features || [])
        .filter((f) => f.attributes.FUNCSTAT !== "S")
        .map((f) => ({ ...toItem(f.attributes), layer: "subdivisions" }));
    }

    // Other states: places inside the county's bounding box, then keep the ones
    // whose internal point is truly inside the county outline.
    const outline = await fetchBoundary({
      id: `county:${county.geoid}`,
      kind: "county",
      geoid: county.geoid,
      layer: "counties",
    });
    if (!outline) return [];
    const [w, s, e, n] = bboxOf(outline);
    const d = await query("places", {
      geometry: `${w},${s},${e},${n}`,
      geometryType: "esriGeometryEnvelope",
      inSR: "4326",
      spatialRel: "esriSpatialRelEnvelopeIntersects",
      where: `STATE='${stateFips}'`,
      outFields: fields,
      returnGeometry: "false",
      orderByFields: "NAME",
      resultRecordCount: "2000",
    });
    return (d.features || [])
      .map((f) => toItem(f.attributes))
      .filter((p) => p.center[0] != null && pointInGeometry(p.center[0], p.center[1], outline));
  });
}

/**
 * Clickable shapes for the map: every state, or every county in a state.
 * @param {"states"|"counties"} what
 * @param {string} [stateFips]
 * @returns {Promise<object>} GeoJSON FeatureCollection; each feature has
 *   properties { id, name, short, geoid }
 */
export function childShapes(what, stateFips) {
  const key = what === "states" ? "shapes:states" : `shapes:counties:${stateFips}`;
  return remember(key, async () => {
    const isStates = what === "states";
    const d = await query(isStates ? "states" : "counties", {
      where: isStates ? "1=1" : `STATE='${stateFips}'`,
      // (STUSAB only exists on the states layer)
      outFields: isStates ? "GEOID,NAME,BASENAME,STUSAB" : "GEOID,NAME,BASENAME",
      returnGeometry: "true",
      maxAllowableOffset: String(isStates ? 0.04 : 0.008),
      resultRecordCount: "500",
      f: "geojson",
    });
    return {
      type: "FeatureCollection",
      features: (d.features || [])
        // keep the 50 states + DC (the layer also has territories)
        .filter((f) => !isStates || /^(0[1-9]|[1-4]\d|5[0-6])$/.test(f.properties.GEOID))
        .map((f) => ({
          type: "Feature",
          geometry: f.geometry,
          properties: {
            id: isStates ? `us-${String(f.properties.STUSAB).toLowerCase()}` : `county:${f.properties.GEOID}`,
            name: f.properties.NAME,
            short: isStates ? f.properties.STUSAB : f.properties.BASENAME,
            geoid: f.properties.GEOID,
          },
        })),
    };
  });
}

// ----- Geometry helpers -----------------------------------------------------

/** [west, south, east, north] of a GeoJSON geometry. */
export function bboxOf(geometry) {
  let w = 180, s = 90, e = -180, n = -90;
  const visit = (c) => {
    if (typeof c[0] === "number") {
      if (c[0] < w) w = c[0];
      if (c[0] > e) e = c[0];
      if (c[1] < s) s = c[1];
      if (c[1] > n) n = c[1];
    } else {
      c.forEach(visit);
    }
  };
  visit(geometry.coordinates);
  return [w, s, e, n];
}

/** Ray-casting point-in-polygon for Polygon / MultiPolygon geometries. */
export function pointInGeometry(lng, lat, geometry) {
  const polys = geometry.type === "Polygon" ? [geometry.coordinates] : geometry.coordinates;
  return polys.some((rings) => {
    if (!inRing(lng, lat, rings[0])) return false;
    for (let i = 1; i < rings.length; i++) if (inRing(lng, lat, rings[i])) return false; // hole
    return true;
  });
}

function inRing(x, y, ring) {
  let inside = false;
  for (let i = 0, j = ring.length - 1; i < ring.length; j = i++) {
    const [xi, yi] = ring[i];
    const [xj, yj] = ring[j];
    if (yi > y !== yj > y && x < ((xj - xi) * (y - yi)) / (yj - yi) + xi) inside = !inside;
  }
  return inside;
}

// data/local-sources.js
// City wards and council districts. The Census doesn't publish these (every
// city draws its own), so they come from each city's open-data portal.
//
// TO ADD A CITY: add one entry to LOCAL_SOURCES below. That's it; the new
// layer appears automatically in the layer dock, the ballot tab and on the map.
//
// Entry fields
//   id        unique id, e.g. "boston-wards"
//   state     2-digit state FIPS ("25" = Massachusetts)
//   city      lowercase city name exactly as the Census spells it ("boston")
//   title     what to call it: "Ward", "City Council District"
//   type      "arcgis" (ArcGIS MapServer / FeatureServer layer) or
//             "socrata" (a Socrata `…/resource/<id>.geojson` dataset)
//   url       the layer URL (arcgis) or dataset .geojson URL (socrata)
//   field     the attribute holding the ward / district number or name
//   source    credit shown in the UI
//
// All entries below were checked to work from a browser (CORS) and to answer
// point-in-polygon queries.

export const LOCAL_SOURCES = [
  {
    id: "boston-wards",
    state: "25",
    city: "boston",
    title: "Ward",
    type: "arcgis",
    url: "https://gis.boston.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Planning/OpenData/MapServer/8",
    field: "WARD",
    source: "City of Boston Open Data",
  },
  {
    id: "boston-council",
    state: "25",
    city: "boston",
    title: "City Council District",
    type: "arcgis",
    url: "https://gis.boston.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Planning/OpenData/MapServer/4",
    field: "DISTRICT",
    source: "City of Boston Open Data",
  },
  {
    id: "chicago-wards",
    state: "17",
    city: "chicago",
    title: "Ward",
    type: "socrata",
    url: "https://data.cityofchicago.org/resource/p293-wvbd.geojson",
    field: "ward",
    source: "City of Chicago Data Portal",
  },
  {
    id: "nyc-council",
    state: "36",
    city: "new york",
    title: "City Council District",
    type: "socrata",
    url: "https://data.cityofnewyork.us/resource/872g-cjhh.geojson",
    field: "coundist",
    source: "NYC Open Data",
  },
];

const SIMPLIFY = 0.0004; // degrees; keeps downloads small

async function fetchJson(url) {
  const ctrl = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => ctrl.abort(), 15000);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(url, { signal: ctrl.signal });
    if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${res.status}`);
    return await res.json();
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

// Returns { value, geometry } for the polygon covering the point, or null.
async function lookup(src, lng, lat) {
  if (src.type === "arcgis") {
    const url = new URL(`${src.url}/query`);
    const params = {
      geometry: `${lng},${lat}`,
      geometryType: "esriGeometryPoint",
      inSR: "4326",
      spatialRel: "esriSpatialRelIntersects",
      outFields: src.field,
      returnGeometry: "true",
      outSR: "4326",
      maxAllowableOffset: String(SIMPLIFY),
      f: "geojson",
    };
    for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(params)) url.searchParams.set(k, v);
    const data = await fetchJson(url.toString());
    const f = data.features?.[0];
    return f ? { value: f.properties[src.field], geometry: f.geometry } : null;
  }

  // Socrata: SoQL with a spatial filter + server-side simplification
  const url = new URL(src.url);
  url.searchParams.set(
    "$select",
    `${src.field}, simplify_preserve_topology(the_geom, ${SIMPLIFY}) as the_geom`
  );
  url.searchParams.set("$where", `intersects(the_geom, 'POINT (${lng} ${lat})')`);
  url.searchParams.set("$limit", "1");
  const data = await fetchJson(url.toString());
  const f = data.features?.[0];
  return f ? { value: f.properties[src.field], geometry: f.geometry } : null;
}

/**
 * Ward / council-district layers for the city at a point (may be empty).
 * @param {{name: string}} city  the "city" jurisdiction
 * @param {string} stateFips
 */
export async function findLocalLayers(city, stateFips, lng, lat) {
  const cityKey = String(city.name || "").trim().toLowerCase();
  const sources = LOCAL_SOURCES.filter((s) => s.state === stateFips && s.city === cityKey);
  const results = await Promise.all(
    sources.map(async (src) => {
      try {
        const hit = await lookup(src, lng, lat);
        if (!hit || hit.value == null || hit.value === "") return null;
        const value = String(hit.value);
        return {
          id: `ward:${src.id}:${value}`,
          kind: "ward",
          geoid: `${src.id}:${value}`,
          state: stateFips,
          name: `${src.title} ${value}`,
          short: `${src.title === "Ward" ? "Ward" : "Dist."} ${value}`,
          type: src.title,
          geometry: hit.geometry,
          center: [lng, lat],
          source: src.source,
        };
      } catch (err) {
        console.warn(`Local source ${src.id} failed:`, err);
        return null;
      }
    })
  );
  return results.filter(Boolean);
}

// data/candidates.js
// The real political data for the globe UI: candidate research profiles and the
// races they are running in.
//
// WHERE THE DATA COMES FROM
//   The candidate research app (Next.js + Supabase, in app/ lib/ supabase/)
//   holds the source of truth:
//     supabase/seed-data/*.json   politician + cited news summary
//     lib/candidate-profiles.ts   curated funding / issues / career / sources / myths
//   `python3 scripts/export_candidates.py` converts both into
//   data/political-data.generated.js, which this module reads. This file ports
//   the merge logic from lib/candidates.ts (Supabase politician + curated
//   profile + news summary, joined by slug), so both apps show the same thing.
//
// TO ADD A CANDIDATE: add supabase/seed-data/<slug>.json (and optionally a
// profile in lib/candidate-profiles.ts), re-run the export script, then list
// them in a race in RACES below.
//
// Shapes are documented in data/types.js (CandidateView, Race).

import {
  POLITICIANS,
  NEWS_SUMMARIES,
  CANDIDATE_PROFILES,
} from "./political-data.generated.js";

// ----- Merge (ported from lib/candidates.ts) ---------------------------------

/** Normalize a year range for matching ("2013–present" ≈ "2013-present"). */
function yearsKey(years) {
  return String(years)
    .replace(/[\u2012-\u2015]/g, "-")
    .replace(/\s+/g, "")
    .toLowerCase();
}

/** First 4-digit year in a period like "1990s-2004", for sorting. */
function startYear(period) {
  const match = /\d{4}/.exec(period);
  return match ? Number(match[0]) : 0;
}

/** Same party label for curated and database records. */
function normalizeParty(party) {
  const value = String(party ?? "").trim();
  return value.toLowerCase() === "democrat" ? "Democratic" : value;
}

/**
 * Database career rows -> Career-tab entries, most recent first. Where a
 * curated profile has a role with the same years, its organization and
 * plain-English description are attached.
 */
function mergeCareer(dbCareer, profileCareer = []) {
  if (dbCareer.length === 0) return profileCareer;
  const byYears = new Map(profileCareer.map((e) => [yearsKey(e.years), e]));
  return [...dbCareer]
    .sort((a, b) => startYear(b.period) - startYear(a.period))
    .map((entry) => {
      const match = byYears.get(yearsKey(entry.period));
      return {
        years: entry.period,
        title: entry.role,
        org: match?.org ?? "",
        description: entry.notes ?? match?.description ?? "",
      };
    });
}

function fromProfileOnly(profile) {
  return {
    slug: profile.slug,
    name: profile.name,
    role: profile.role,
    party: normalizeParty(profile.party),
    bio: null,
    photo: profile.photo ?? null,
    status: profile.status ?? null,
    openSecretsUrl: profile.openSecretsUrl ?? null,
    career: profile.career ?? [],
    funding: profile.funding ?? null,
    opinions: profile.opinions ?? [],
    sources: profile.sources ?? [],
    misconceptions: profile.misconceptions ?? [],
    news: null,
  };
}

function fromPolitician(p, profile, news) {
  const dbCareer = Array.isArray(p.career_history) ? p.career_history : [];
  return {
    slug: p.slug,
    name: p.name,
    role: p.current_office ?? profile?.role ?? "",
    party: normalizeParty(p.party ?? profile?.party),
    bio: p.bio ?? null,
    photo: profile?.photo ?? null,
    status: profile?.status ?? null,
    openSecretsUrl: profile?.openSecretsUrl ?? null,
    career: mergeCareer(dbCareer, profile?.career),
    funding: profile?.funding ?? null,
    opinions: profile?.opinions ?? [],
    sources: profile?.sources ?? [],
    misconceptions: profile?.misconceptions ?? [],
    news: news ?? null,
  };
}

function buildViews() {
  const profiles = new Map(CANDIDATE_PROFILES.map((c) => [c.slug, c]));
  const views = POLITICIANS.map((p) => {
    const profile = profiles.get(p.slug);
    profiles.delete(p.slug);
    return fromPolitician(p, profile, NEWS_SUMMARIES[p.slug]);
  });
  // Curated profiles that don't have a politician row yet.
  for (const profile of profiles.values()) views.push(fromProfileOnly(profile));
  return views.sort((a, b) => a.name.localeCompare(b.name));
}

const VIEWS = buildViews();
const BY_SLUG = new Map(VIEWS.map((v) => [v.slug, v]));

// ----- Lookups ----------------------------------------------------------------

/** Every candidate profile we have, A to Z. */
export function getCandidates() {
  return VIEWS;
}

export function getCandidate(slug) {
  return BY_SLUG.get(slug) || null;
}

/** Name / office / party search for the search box. */
export function searchCandidates(query, limit = 4) {
  const q = String(query || "").trim().toLowerCase();
  if (q.length < 2) return [];
  return VIEWS.filter((c) =>
    [c.name, c.role, c.party].some((field) => String(field || "").toLowerCase().includes(q))
  ).slice(0, limit);
}

/** Initials for the avatar fallback ("Maura Healey" -> "MH"). */
export function initials(name) {
  return String(name)
    .split(/\s+/)
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((w) => w[0])
    .join("")
    .slice(0, 2)
    .toUpperCase();
}

// ----- Races: who is running for what -----------------------------------------
//
// This is the link between the candidate research data and the ballot. Each
// race lists candidate SLUGS (from supabase/seed-data); names and parties are
// read from the profiles above so there is only one place to edit them.
//
// Source of the pairings: the candidate bios in supabase/seed-data/*.json
// (Healey vs. Minogue for governor; Markey vs. Deaton for U.S. Senate).

const GENERAL_ELECTION_2026 = "2026-11-03";
const RESEARCH_SOURCE = "Candidate research (Oct 2026)";

export const RACES = [
  {
    id: "ma-governor-2026",
    state: "MA",
    office: "Governor of Massachusetts",
    kind: "state",
    category: "executive",
    term: "4 years",
    electionDate: GENERAL_ELECTION_2026,
    candidates: ["maura-healey", "mike-minogue"],
    description: "Statewide race for governor on the November 2026 ballot.",
  },
  {
    id: "ma-senate-2026",
    state: "MA",
    office: "U.S. Senator (Massachusetts)",
    kind: "state",
    category: "legislative",
    term: "6 years",
    electionDate: GENERAL_ELECTION_2026,
    candidates: ["ed-markey", "john-deaton"],
    description: "Statewide race for one of Massachusetts's two U.S. Senate seats.",
  },
];

/**
 * Race objects (see data/types.js) for a state, with real candidates. Each
 * candidate carries a `slug` so the UI can open their profile.
 * @param {string} stateCode  USPS code, e.g. "MA"
 */
export function racesForState(stateCode) {
  return RACES.filter((r) => r.state === stateCode).map((r) => ({
    id: r.id,
    office: r.office,
    kind: r.kind,
    category: r.category,
    term: r.term,
    electionDate: r.electionDate,
    description: r.description,
    source: RESEARCH_SOURCE,
    candidates: r.candidates.map((slug) => {
      const c = BY_SLUG.get(slug);
      return { slug, name: c ? c.name : slug, party: c ? c.party : null };
    }),
  }));
}

/** True when we have real candidate data for this state's statewide races. */
export function hasRealRaces(stateCode) {
  return RACES.some((r) => r.state === stateCode);
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Export the teammates' political data for the globe UI.

The candidate research app (Next.js + Supabase) keeps its data in two places:

  supabase/seed-data/*.json      politician + cited news summary (the same files
                                 that build supabase/news_seed.sql)
  lib/candidate-profiles.ts      hand-curated funding / issues / career / sources
                                 / myths / status, keyed by slug

The globe UI is a static site (no build step), so it can't import TypeScript or
query Supabase without keys. This script turns both sources into ONE plain
JavaScript module the browser can import directly:

  data/political-data.generated.js

Run it whenever those source files change:

  python3 scripts/export_candidates.py

Nothing in the generated file is edited by hand. Fix data in the source files,
then re-run this script.
"""

import json
import re
import sys
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from pathlib import Path

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
SEED_DIR = ROOT / "supabase" / "seed-data"
PROFILES_TS = ROOT / "lib" / "candidate-profiles.ts"
BUILD_SEED = ROOT / "supabase" / "build-news-seed.mjs"
OUT = ROOT / "data" / "political-data.generated.js"

CITATION_FIELDS = ("n", "title", "url", "source", "published_at")


def fail(msg):
    print(f"error: {msg}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(1)


def model_label():
    """Reuse the label the Supabase seed builder stamps on its summaries."""
    m = re.search(r'MODEL_LABEL\s*=\s*"([^"]+)"', BUILD_SEED.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    return m.group(1) if m else "Research summary"


def load_seed(generated_at):
    politicians, news = [], {}
    files = sorted(SEED_DIR.glob("*.json"))
    if not files:
        fail(f"no seed files found in {SEED_DIR}")
    label = model_label()
    for path in files:
        d = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        p = d["politician"]
        if not p.get("slug") or not p.get("name"):
            fail(f"{path.name}: politician.slug and name are required")
        politicians.append(p)
        citations = [{k: c.get(k) for k in CITATION_FIELDS} for c in d["citations"]]
        news[p["slug"]] = {
            "summary": d["summary"],
            "citations": citations,
            "article_count": len(citations),
            "model": label,
            "generated_at": generated_at,
        }
    return politicians, news


def load_profiles():
    """candidate-profiles.ts is plain object literals; only the import line and
    the type annotation on the export are TypeScript."""
    ts = PROFILES_TS.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    ts = re.sub(r"^import type [^;]+;\s*$", "", ts, flags=re.M)
    ts, n = re.subn(
        r"export const CANDIDATE_PROFILES\s*:\s*CandidateProfile\[\]\s*=",
        "export const CANDIDATE_PROFILES =",
        ts,
    )
    if n != 1:
        fail("could not find `export const CANDIDATE_PROFILES: CandidateProfile[] =` in candidate-profiles.ts")
    # Any other TypeScript-only syntax would break the browser import.
    for pattern, what in (
        (r"\bas (const|[A-Z]\w*)\b", "`as` cast"),
        (r"\bsatisfies\b", "`satisfies`"),
        (r"\binterface\b", "`interface`"),
    ):
        if re.search(pattern, ts):
            fail(f"candidate-profiles.ts uses TypeScript-only syntax ({what}); extend export_candidates.py")
    return ts.strip()


def main():
    generated_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).replace(microsecond=0).isoformat().replace("+00:00", "Z")
    politicians, news = load_seed(generated_at)
    profiles_js = load_profiles()

        "// Sources: supabase/seed-data/*.json and lib/candidate-profiles.ts",
        "// Refresh:  python3 scripts/export_candidates.py",
        "",
        f"export const GENERATED_AT = {json.dumps(generated_at)};",
        "",
        "// Politicians + cited news summaries (same content as supabase/news_seed.sql)",
        f"export const POLITICIANS = {json.dumps(politicians, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)};",
        "",
        f"export const NEWS_SUMMARIES = {json.dumps(news, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)};",
        "",
        "// Hand-curated research profiles (verbatim from lib/candidate-profiles.ts)",
        profiles_js,
        "",
    ]
    OUT.write_text("\n".join(parts), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"wrote {OUT.relative_to(ROOT)}  ({OUT.stat().st_size // 1024} KB)")
    print(f"  politicians: {len(politicians)}  news summaries: {len(news)}")
    profile_count = len(re.findall(r"^\s*slug:", profiles_js, flags=re.M))
    print(f"  curated profiles: {profile_count}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

// ----- Index + parent links -------------------------------------------------

const INDEX = new Map();

function register(n, parent = null) {
  n.parent = parent;
  INDEX.set(n.id, n);
  for (const child of n.children) register(child, n);
}
register(PLACES);

// Which layer of government a place level corresponds to (for races/events
// that don't say so explicitly).
const LEVEL_TO_KIND = {
  country: "country",
  state: "state",
  county: "county",
  city: "city",
  district: "ward",
};

// ----- Lookup helpers -------------------------------------------------------

export function findNodeById(id) {
  return INDEX.get(id) || null;
}

// Chain of nodes from the root (Earth) down to and including the node. Used for
// breadcrumbs. Empty array if the id is unknown.
export function pathToNode(id) {
  let n = INDEX.get(id);
  const path = [];
  while (n) {
    path.unshift(n);
    n = n.parent;
  }
  return path;
}

// Fallback used only when reverse geocoding is unavailable: given a [lng, lat]
// find the deepest curated node whose bbox contains the point.
export function resolveByCoords(lng, lat, n = PLACES, trail = []) {
  const nextTrail = [...trail, n];
  for (const child of n.children) {
    if (bboxContains(child.bbox, lng, lat)) {
      return resolveByCoords(lng, lat, child, nextTrail);
    }
  }
  return nextTrail;
}

function bboxContains(bbox, lng, lat) {
  if (!bbox) return false;
  const [w, s, e, n] = bbox;
  return lng >= w && lng <= e && lat >= s && lat <= n;
}

// ancestor (state governor applies to each city in the state, etc.).
export function racesForNode(id) {
  const out = [];
  for (const n of pathToNode(id)) {
    for (const race of n.races) {
      out.push({
        ...race,
        kind: race.kind || LEVEL_TO_KIND[n.level],
        scopeName: n.name,
        scopeLevel: n.level,
      });
    }
  }
  return out;
}

// Upcoming events that apply to a node (own + inherited), soonest first.
export function eventsForNode(id, now = new Date()) {
  const out = [];
  for (const n of pathToNode(id)) {
    for (const evt of n.events) {
      const endsAt = evt.end
        ? new Date(evt.end)
        : new Date(new Date(evt.start).getTime() + 3 * 3600 * 1000);
      if (endsAt < now) continue; // already over
      out.push({
        ...evt,
        kind: evt.kind || LEVEL_TO_KIND[n.level],
        scopeName: n.name,
        scopeLevel: n.level,
      });
    }
  }
  out.sort((a, b) => new Date(a.start) - new Date(b.start));
  return out;

  let parent = PLACES;
  for (const n of path) {

// Lowercase, strip accents and generic suffixes so "Fort Bend County",
// "Fort Bend" and "fort bend" all compare equal.
export function normalizeName(str) {
  return String(str || "")
    .normalize("NFD")
    .replace(/\p{M}/gu, "")
    .toLowerCase()
    .replace(/\b(county|parish|borough|city of|town of|municipality of)\b/g, " ")
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, " ")
    .trim();
}

function nameMatches(n, normalized) {
  if (normalizeName(n.name) === normalized) return true;
  return (n.aliases || []).some((a) => normalizeName(a) === normalized);
}

function findChild(parent, name, level, code) {
  const target = normalizeName(name);
  return (
    parent.children.find(
      (c) =>
        c.level === level &&
        ((code && c.code && c.code.toUpperCase() === code.toUpperCase()) ||
          nameMatches(c, target))
    ) || null
  );

// Search the whole subtree (used when a result skips the county level but we
// already have that city filed under a county).
function findInSubtree(root, name, level) {
  const target = normalizeName(name);
  const stack = [...root.children];
  while (stack.length) {
    const n = stack.pop();
    if (n.level === level && nameMatches(n, target)) return n;
    stack.push(...n.children);
  }
  return null;
}

function slugify(str) {
  return normalizeName(str).replace(/ /g, "-") || "unknown";
}

function addDynamicChild(parent, fields) {
  const child = node({
    id: `${parent.id}/${slugify(fields.name)}`,
    dynamic: true,
    ...fields,
  });
  child.parent = parent;
  parent.children.push(child);
  INDEX.set(child.id, child);
  return child;
}

// the first time someone opens a state or county (see loadChildren in
// data/civic.js) and added to the tree here. Curated nodes above are reused
// (matched by Census id, then by name) so their sample races/events stay.

function findChildByGeoid(parent, geoid) {
  return parent.children.find((c) => c.geoid === geoid) || null;
}

// Find-or-create a child. `item`: { geoid, name, center, type?, layer? }.
function upsertChild(parent, item, level) {
  let child =
    findChildByGeoid(parent, item.geoid) ||
    findChild(parent, item.name, level, null);
  if (child) {
    if (!child.geoid) child.geoid = item.geoid;
    if (item.layer) child.layer = item.layer;
    if (item.type) child.type = item.type;
    return child;
  }
  // Ids must be unique tree-wide. A city that sits in several counties (New
  // York City) gets one node per county.
  let id = `${level}:${item.geoid}`;
  if (INDEX.has(id)) id = `${id}@${parent.id}`;
  child = node({
    id,
    geoid: item.geoid,
    name: item.name,
    level,
    center: item.center,
    layer: item.layer,
    type: item.type,
    dynamic: true,
  });
  child.parent = parent;
  parent.children.push(child);
  INDEX.set(child.id, child);
  return child;
}

 * @param {object} parent
 * @param {{geoid: string, name: string, center: number[], type?: string, layer?: string}[]} items
 * @param {"county"|"city"} level
 */
export function attachChildren(parent, items, level) {
  const nodes = items.map((it) => upsertChild(parent, it, level));
  parent.childrenState = "loaded";
  return nodes;
}

 * @param {object[]} stack
 * @param {"state"|"county"|"city"} [downTo]  deepest level to go to
 * @returns {object[]} path from Earth down; just [Earth] if not in the U.S.
 */
export function pathFromStack(stack, downTo = "city") {
  const stateJ = stack.find((j) => j.kind === "state");
  const state = stateJ && usa.children.find((s) => s.code === stateJ.short);
  if (!state) return [PLACES];
  const path = [PLACES, usa, state];
  if (downTo === "state") return path;

  const countyJ = stack.find((j) => j.kind === "county");
  if (!countyJ) return path;
  const county = upsertChild(
    state,
    { geoid: countyJ.geoid, name: countyJ.name, center: countyJ.center, layer: "counties" },
    "county"
  );
  path.push(county);
  if (downTo === "county") return path;

  const cityJ = stack.find((j) => j.kind === "city");
  if (!cityJ) return path;
  const city = upsertChild(
    county,
    {
      geoid: cityJ.geoid,
      name: cityJ.name,
      center: cityJ.center,
      type: cityJ.type,
      layer: cityJ.layer,
    },
    "city"
  );
  path.push(city);
  return path;
}

// Show "Fort Bend County" rather than "Fort Bend" for U.S. counties.
function countyDisplayName(name, countryCode) {
  if (countryCode === "US" && !/\b(county|parish|borough|census area)\b/i.test(name)) {
    return `${name} County`;
  }
  return name;
}

/**
 * Turn a geocoder result into a path of place nodes, creating any county /
 * city / district nodes that don't exist yet. Returns the path from Earth down
 * to the deepest place we could identify (always at least [Earth]).
 *
 * United States only: results from other countries return just [Earth].
 * All 50 states + DC always exist (data/us-states.js), so only counties,
 * cities and districts are ever created at runtime.
 *
 * @param {object} desc - normalized geocoder result (see js/geocode.js):
 *   { type, name, country, countryCode, state, county, city, lng, lat, extent }
 */
export function ensurePath(desc) {
  const path = [PLACES];
  if (desc.countryCode !== "US") return path;

  const here = [desc.lng, desc.lat];
  const isType = (t) => desc.type === t;
  path.push(usa);

  // State (always pre-built; never created at runtime)
  const stateName = isType("state") ? desc.name : desc.state;
  const state = stateName ? findChild(usa, stateName, "state", null) : null;
  if (!state) return path; // the country itself, or a state we can't match
  path.push(state);
  const afterState = state;

  // County
  const countyRaw = isType("county") ? desc.name : desc.county;
  let county = null;
  if (countyRaw) {
    const countyName = countyDisplayName(countyRaw, desc.countryCode);
    county = findChild(state, countyName, "county", null);
    if (!county) {
      county = addDynamicChild(state, { name: countyName, level: "county", center: here });
    }
    path.push(county);
  }

  // City / town
  const cityName = isType("city") ? desc.name : desc.city;
  let city = null;
  if (cityName) {
    city = county ? findChild(county, cityName, "city", null) : null;
    if (!city && !county) {
      // Result had no county: reuse the city if we already have it somewhere
      // under this state, and fix up the path to its real ancestors.
      const existing = findInSubtree(afterState, cityName, "city");
      if (existing) {
        const full = pathToNode(existing.id);
        path.length = 0;
        path.push(...full);
        city = existing;
      }
    }
    if (!city) {
      city = addDynamicChild(county || afterState, {
        name: cityName,
        level: "city",
        center: here,
      });
      if (!path.includes(city)) path.push(city);
    } else if (!path.includes(city)) {
      path.push(city);
    }
  }

  // District (e.g. a neighbourhood), only when it differs from the city above.
  if (isType("district") && city && normalizeName(desc.name) !== normalizeName(city.name)) {
    let district = findChild(city, desc.name, "district", null);
    if (!district) {
      district = addDynamicChild(city, { name: desc.name, level: "district", center: here });
    }
    path.push(district);
  }

  // Give the node we ended on the exact point/extent from the search so the
  // camera lands precisely (only for nodes made from search, never curated).
  const target = path[path.length - 1];
  if (target.dynamic) {
    target.center = here;
    if (desc.extent && isAdminType(desc.type)) target.extent = desc.extent;
  }
  return path;
}

function isAdminType(type) {
  return ["state", "county", "city", "district"].includes(type);
}

// data/races.js
// Factory helpers that build race objects. Keeping the shape in one place makes
// it easy to (a) keep sample data consistent and (b) see the target schema when
// wiring a real data source.
//
// Race shape (full reference in data/types.js):
//   id           unique-ish id for keys
//   office       the office being contested ("Governor of Texas", ...)
//   kind         WHICH LAYER OF GOVERNMENT decides it: a key of KINDS in
//                data/kinds.js ("country" | "state" | "congress" | "senate" |
//                "house" | "county" | "city" | "school" | "ward"). The ballot
//                tab groups races by this.
//   category     secondary grouping/icon: "executive" | "legislative" | "local" |
//                "education" | "measure"
//   term         "4 years" (optional)
//   electionDate "YYYY-MM-DD" of the next election, or null when it varies
//   candidates   [{ name, party }]
//   description  optional plain-language context
//
// ALL CANDIDATES BELOW ARE PLACEHOLDERS ("Candidate A"). Replace with real data
// from your data source (see data/civic.js).

export const MIDTERM_2026 = "2026-11-03"; // General Election Day, Nov 3 2026
export const PRESIDENTIAL_2028 = "2028-11-07"; // General Election Day, Nov 7 2028

let _seq = 0;
const uid = (prefix) => `${prefix}-${++_seq}`;

const TWO = (a, b, partyA = "Party 1", partyB = "Party 2") => [
  { name: a, party: partyA },
  { name: b, party: partyB },
];

export function presidentialRace() {
  return {
    id: uid("pres"),
    office: "President of the United States",
    kind: "country",
    category: "executive",
    term: "4 years",
    electionDate: PRESIDENTIAL_2028,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate A", "Candidate B"),
    description:
      "National election, next held in 2028. Applies to every U.S. location.",
  };
}

export function makeGovernorRace(stateName) {
  return {
    id: uid("gov"),
    office: `Governor of ${stateName}`,
    kind: "state",
    category: "executive",
    term: "4 years",
    electionDate: MIDTERM_2026,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate C", "Candidate D"),
    description: `Statewide executive race for ${stateName}.`,
  };
}

export function makeSenateRace(stateName) {
  return {
    id: uid("sen"),
    office: `U.S. Senator (${stateName})`,
    kind: "state",
    category: "legislative",
    term: "6 years",
    electionDate: MIDTERM_2026,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate E", "Candidate F"),
    description: `Represents all of ${stateName} in the U.S. Senate.`,
  };
}

// One race per U.S. House district. `districtCode` like "TX-22".
export function makeHouseRace(districtCode) {
  return {
    id: uid("house"),
    office: `U.S. House, District ${districtCode}`,
    kind: "congress",
    category: "legislative",
    term: "2 years",
    electionDate: MIDTERM_2026,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate G", "Candidate H"),
    description: `Represents congressional district ${districtCode} in Washington, D.C.`,
  };
}

// State legislature: `chamber` is "senate" or "house"; `districtName` is the
// district's name from the Census ("State Senate District 17").
export function makeStateLegislatorRace(chamber, districtName, stateName) {
  const upper = chamber === "senate";
  return {
    id: uid(upper ? "ssen" : "shouse"),
    office: `${upper ? "State Senator" : "State Representative"}, ${districtName}`,
    kind: chamber,
    category: "legislative",
    term: "varies by state",
    electionDate: null,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate P", "Candidate Q"),
    description: `Represents this district in the ${stateName} ${
      upper ? "Senate" : "House (lower chamber)"
    }. Terms and election years vary by state.`,
  };
}

export function makeCountyRace(office, countyName, description) {
  return {
    id: uid("county"),
    office,
    kind: "county",
    category: "local",
    term: "4 years",
    electionDate: MIDTERM_2026,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate N", "Candidate O"),
    description: description || `County-level office for ${countyName}.`,
  };
}

export function makeMayorRace(cityName) {
  return {
    id: uid("mayor"),
    office: `Mayor of ${cityName}`,
    kind: "city",
    category: "local",
    term: "varies",
    electionDate: null,
    candidates: TWO("Candidate I", "Candidate J", "Nonpartisan", "Nonpartisan"),
    description: `Head of the ${cityName} city government. Election dates vary by city.`,
  };
}

// School governing board. `boardName` examples: "Boston School Committee",
// "Fort Bend ISD Board of Trustees".
export function makeSchoolBoardRace(boardName, whatItGoverns) {
  return {
    id: uid("school"),
    office: boardName,
    kind: "school",
    category: "education",
    term: "varies",
    electionDate: null,
    candidates: [
      { name: "Candidate K", party: "Nonpartisan" },
      { name: "Candidate L", party: "Nonpartisan" },
      { name: "Candidate M", party: "Nonpartisan" },
    ],
    description: `Governs ${whatItGoverns || "the local public schools"}.`,

// `kind` = the layer that votes on it (default "state").
export function makeBallotMeasure(title, scopeName, summary, kind = "state") {
  return {
    id: uid("measure"),
    office: title,
    kind,
    category: "measure",
    term: null,
    electionDate: MIDTERM_2026,
    candidates: [
      { name: "Yes", party: null },
      { name: "No", party: null },
    ],
    description: `${summary} (${scopeName}).`,
  };
}

// Visual metadata per category: used for the small tag on each race card.
export const CATEGORY_META = {

  legislative: { label: "Legislative", icon: "⚖️", color: "#7c3aed" },

};

// data/events.js
// Factory helpers for civic events (town halls, meetings, debates, voter
// registration drives, election days, ...).
//
// Event shape:
//   id          - unique-ish id
//   title       - short name
//   kind        - OPTIONAL layer of government that holds it (a key of KINDS in
//                 data/kinds.js, e.g. "city", "school", "congress"). If omitted,
//                 it is taken from the place the event is attached to.
//   type        - key of EVENT_TYPES below
//   start       - ISO 8601 date-time string (local time of the event)
//   end         - optional ISO string
//   venue       - where it happens ("City Hall, Council Chambers")
//   virtual     - true if it can be joined online
//   description - one or two plain-language sentences
//   url         - optional link for details / RSVP
//   source      - "sample" for mock data; real feeds should set their own name
//
// The sample events use dates RELATIVE TO TODAY (see daysFromNow) so a demo
// never shows a stale calendar. Real feeds should return real dates.
// Election Day events use the real general-election date.

export const EVENT_TYPES = {
  townhall: { label: "Town hall", icon: "🎤", color: "#b45309" },
  meeting: { label: "Public meeting", icon: "🏛️", color: "#1d4ed8" },
  debate: { label: "Debate / forum", icon: "💬", color: "#7c3aed" },
  voting: { label: "Voting", icon: "🗳️", color: "#be123c" },
  hearing: { label: "Public hearing", icon: "📣", color: "#0e7490" },
  community: { label: "Community", icon: "🤝", color: "#15803d" },
};

let _seq = 0;
const uid = () => `evt-${++_seq}`;

// ISO string for N days from today at the given local hour/minute.
export function daysFromNow(days, hour = 18, minute = 30) {
  const d = new Date();
  d.setDate(d.getDate() + days);
  d.setHours(hour, minute, 0, 0);
  return toLocalIso(d);
}

// Build an ISO-like local string without converting to UTC.
export function toLocalIso(d) {
  const p = (n) => String(n).padStart(2, "0");
  return `${d.getFullYear()}-${p(d.getMonth() + 1)}-${p(d.getDate())}T${p(
    d.getHours()
  )}:${p(d.getMinutes())}:00`;
}

export function makeEvent(fields) {
  return {
    id: uid(),
    type: "meeting",
    virtual: false,
    source: "sample",
    ...fields,
  };
}

export function electionDayEvent(date = "2026-11-03", scopeLabel = "") {
  return makeEvent({
    title: `General Election Day${scopeLabel ? ` (${scopeLabel})` : ""}`,
    type: "voting",
    kind: "country",
    start: `${date}T07:00:00`,
    end: `${date}T20:00:00`,
    venue: "Your assigned polling place (check your local election office)",
    description:
      "Polls are open on Election Day. Hours vary by state, so confirm yours with your local election office.",
  });
}

// data/levels.js
// The administrative hierarchy the globe drills through.
// The order here drives breadcrumb depth, zoom behavior, and "move up / down" logic.
//
// Each level has:
//   key    - stable identifier used in code
//   label  - plain-language name shown in the UI
//   noun   - lowercase noun used in sentences ("Choose a state or region…")
//   zoom   - fallback MapLibre zoom when the camera lands on this level
//            (nodes with a `bbox` are framed to fit instead; see js/globe.js)
//
// SCOPE: the app is United States only for now, so the tree is
//   World -> United States -> State -> County -> City -> District.
// To support other countries later, add a "continent" level between globe and
// country here, add continent nodes in data/places.js, and widen the filters in
// js/geocode.js. Teams can also insert levels (e.g. "ward" below city) without
// touching the map or UI code.

export const LEVELS = [
  { key: "globe", label: "World", noun: "world", zoom: 1.5 },
  { key: "country", label: "Country", noun: "country", zoom: 3.4 },
  { key: "state", label: "State / Region", noun: "state or region", zoom: 6 },
  { key: "county", label: "County", noun: "county", zoom: 8.5 },
  { key: "city", label: "City / Town", noun: "city or town", zoom: 10.5 },
  { key: "district", label: "District", noun: "district", zoom: 12 },
];

// Fast lookups by key and by index.
export const LEVEL_INDEX = Object.fromEntries(
  LEVELS.map((lvl, i) => [lvl.key, i])
);

export function levelByKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  return i === undefined ? null : LEVELS[i];
}

export function nextLevelKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  if (i === undefined || i >= LEVELS.length - 1) return null;
  return LEVELS[i + 1].key;
}

export function prevLevelKey(key) {
  const i = LEVEL_INDEX[key];
  if (i === undefined || i <= 0) return null;
  return LEVELS[i - 1].key;
}

// data/types.js
// One place that documents every data shape the UI understands. Nothing here
// runs: these are JSDoc typedefs for people (and AI prompts) to point at, e.g.
// "add a dataset of school board races shaped like Race in data/types.js".
//
// Rule of thumb: the UI never needs to change when data is added. It renders
// whatever Place / Race / Event objects it is given.

/**
 * A place in the hierarchy: World > United States > State > County > City > District.
 * Defined in data/places.js (curated) or created at runtime from search results.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Place
 * @property {string}   id        Unique and stable, e.g. "tx-sugarland" or "us-tx".
 * @property {string}   name      Display name, e.g. "Sugar Land".
 * @property {"globe"|"country"|"state"|"county"|"city"|"district"} level
 *                                 See data/levels.js.
 * @property {[number, number]} center  [lng, lat] the camera flies to.
 * @property {number}   [zoom]    Camera zoom override (else the level default).
 * @property {[number, number, number, number]} [extent]
 *                                 [west, south, east, north]; camera frames this
 *                                 box instead of using zoom (search results).
 * @property {[number, number, number, number]} [bbox]
 *                                 Offline-only fallback for matching GPS points.
 * @property {string[]} [aliases] Other names that should match this place.
 * @property {string}   [code]    "US" for the country, USPS code for states ("TX").
 * @property {string}   [geoid]   Census id (state "48", county "48157", city
 *                                 "4870808"). Lets Census data merge with curated nodes.
 * @property {Race[]}   races     Races DECIDED at this place (inherited downward).
 * @property {Event[]}  events    Events at this place (inherited downward).
 * @property {Place[]}  children  Places one level down.
 * @property {Place}    [parent]  Set automatically; do not write by hand.
 * @property {boolean}  [dynamic] True if created at runtime from a search.
 */

/**
 * Something on the ballot: a candidate race or a ballot question.
 * Built with the factories in data/races.js, or write the object directly.
 * Shown in the "On the ballot" tab, grouped by `category`.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Race
 * @property {string} id
 * @property {string} office        "Governor of Texas", "Mayor of Medford", ...
 * @property {"country"|"state"|"congress"|"senate"|"house"|"county"|"city"|"school"|"ward"|"precinct"} kind
 *                                   WHICH LAYER OF GOVERNMENT decides it
 *                                   (KINDS in data/kinds.js). The Ballot tab is
 *                                   grouped by this, and it picks the color.
 * @property {"executive"|"legislative"|"local"|"education"|"measure"} category
 *                                   Small tag + icon on the card
 *                                   (CATEGORY_META in data/races.js).
 * @property {string} [jurisdictionId]  Set on races generated for a district,
 *                                   e.g. "congress:4822".
 * @property {{name: string, party: string|null, slug?: string}[]} candidates
 *                                   A `slug` makes the candidate clickable: it
 *                                   opens their profile (CandidateView).
 * @property {string|null} [term]    "4 years"; null for ballot questions.
 * @property {string|null} electionDate  "YYYY-MM-DD" or null if it varies.
 * @property {{name: string, party: string|null}[]} candidates
 *                                   For ballot questions use Yes / No.
 * @property {string} [description]  One or two plain-language sentences.
 * @property {string} [scopeName]    Added automatically: the Place that decides it.
 */

/**
 * A civic event: town hall, public meeting, debate/forum, voting date, ...
 * Built with makeEvent() in data/events.js. Shown in "Events & town halls",
 * soonest first; past events are hidden automatically.
 *
 * @typedef {Object} Event
 * @property {string} id
 * @property {string} title
 * @property {"townhall"|"meeting"|"debate"|"voting"|"hearing"|"community"} type
 *                                   Controls icon and color (EVENT_TYPES in
